title: Substitute SQL duplicates the existing idempotent insert instead of reusing it — the live-slot ON CONFLICT predicate is now maintained in three places
evidence: substitute_reference_call.sql lines 15-27: INSERT INTO reference_call (application_id, ref_slot, owner_label, contact_name, contact_email, contact_phone, next_attempt_at) ... ON CONFLICT (application_id, ref_slot, owner_label) WHERE status NOT IN ('form_completed','unreachable','refused','objected','manual_recorded','failed','completed','partial') DO NOTHING — byte-for-byte the same column list, NULLIF($n,'') pattern and conflict predicate as insert_reference_call_if_absent.sql (VALUES ($1,$2,$3,$4,NULLIF($5,''),NULLIF($6,''),now()) ... ON CONFLICT (application_id, ref_slot, owner_label) WHERE status NOT IN (...same set...) DO NOTHING). The PR's own spec (spec-rc4-3-row-actions.md, OWNS #1, in this chunk) states substitution inserts 'via the existing insert_reference_call_if_absent (partial unique index — the prior terminal row doesn't occupy the slot; a double-click conflicts → no-op, 200)' — the implementation does NOT call that query; it inlines a bespoke CTE copy. The conflict predicate therefore exists in three places: the index definition in supabase/migrations/20260731222000_create_reference_call.sql (~line 138), insert_reference_call_if_absent.sql (whose own comment warns the predicate must be copied VERBATIM from the index 'so Postgres can infer the index for ON CONFLICT'), and the new CTE. Postgres raises an error (not a silent no-op) when an ON CONFLICT predicate does not exactly match an existing partial index, so any future drift between the three copies would turn substitution double-submits into 500s instead of the designed 200 no-op. Verified today the three predicates match verbatim, so current behaviour is correct — this is a maintainability + spec-vs-code drift note, not a functional defect.
recommendation: Either have substitute_reference_call.sql reference the existing insert path (e.g. a CTE around the existing query cannot work — it is a standalone INSERT — so the realistic fix is a shared comment/constant discipline or a comment in both files pointing at each other), or amend the spec/implementation notes to state the insert is inlined by design and that the predicate is copied verbatim from idx_reference_call_live in three places.

title: Spec Files list names files that don't exist under that name and miscounts new vs edited SQL
evidence: spec-rc4-3-row-actions.md, Files section: '- NEW: ... update_application_referee_trio.sql ...' — no such file exists in the worktree; the code ships three per-slot queries: server/src/reference_checks/sql/update_application_referee_trio_landlord.sql, update_application_referee_trio_character.sql, update_application_referee_trio_employer.sql (all consumed by actions_handler.gleam lines 610-630, selected by ref_slot). Completion Notes section states '7 new SQL queries' while the diff adds 4 new queries (take_over_reference_call.sql, correct_reference_call.sql, substitute_reference_call.sql + the three trio updates and the exhaustion edit make 4 new + 3 expand-only edits: list_reference_calls_for_detail.sql, find_reference_call_by_send_ref.sql, get_form_context_by_form_token.sql). Also Dev Notes state the substitution insert goes 'via the existing insert_reference_call_if_absent' while the implementation inlines it (see first finding). Internal documentation drift only — no product impact; the code itself is consistent and all referenced real files exist.
recommendation: Update the spec artifact to the shipped names (three per-slot trio-update files) and to the accurate new-vs-edited SQL count.
